question: Among the patients followed at the outpatient clinic, how many of them have a normal level of alkaliphophatase?
evidence: followed at the outpatient clinic refers to Admission = '-'; normal level of alkaliphophatase refers to ALP < 300;
clarification: Count each distinct ID only once.
gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.ALP < 300 AND T1.Admission = '-'
gold0: SELECT COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.ALP < 300 AND T1.Admission = '-'

d.request: Among the patients followed at the outpatient clinic (Admission = '-'), how many have a normal alkaline phosphatase level (ALP < 300), counting each distinct patient ID only once?
d.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT P.ID) FROM Patient AS P INNER JOIN Laboratory AS L ON P.ID = L.ID WHERE P.Admission = '-' AND L.ALP < 300

b.request: How many distinct patients (counting each ID once) with Admission = '-' have at least one Laboratory record with ALP < 300?
b.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT P.ID) FROM Patient P INNER JOIN Laboratory L ON P.ID = L.ID WHERE P.Admission = '-' AND L.ALP < 300
